entities.name: Al-Mundhir III ibn al-Harith
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Al-Mundhir ibn al-Ḥārith, known in Byzantine sources as Flavios Alamoundaros, was the king of the Ghassanid Arabs from 569 to circa 581. A son of al-Harith ibn Jabalah, he succeeded his father both in the kingship over his tribe and as the chief of the Byzantine Empire's Arab clients and allies in the East, with the rank of patricius. Despite his victories over the rival Persian-backed Lakhmids, throughout Mundhir's reign his relations with Byzantium were lukewarm due to his staunch Miaphysitism.
